articles.title: Here are the brands bringing ads to ChatGPT
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched its advertising pilot in ChatGPT, and several brands, including Target, Audible, Adobe, and others, have announced plans to participate.
articles.body: OpenAI officially launched its advertising pilot in ChatGPT, leaving us with a better idea of the kinds of products we might see stuffed beneath our conversations with the AI chatbot. Several companies have announced plans to show ads inside ChatGPT — placements that will reportedly cost them a pretty penny — ranging from major retailers like Target to automakers like Ford and Mazda. You’ll only see ads in ChatGPT if you’re a free user or subscribed to its cheaper $8 / month Go plan. OpenAI has said it will “clearly” label the ads and that they won’t influence ChatGPT’s response. Here are all the brands that we know are partnering with OpenAI so far. Target Target says in an announcement that it will use ads in ChatGPT to help users “discover products, deals and inspiration that meet what they’re seeking at that moment.” It notes that ads will appear based on keywords that appear in a user’s ChatGPT prompt. As an example, Target says someone using ChatGPT to look for “countertop cooking appliances that make everyday meals more convenient” might see an ad for an air fryer from Target. Adobe Adobe is planning to show ads for its AI-powered document editor, Acrobat Studio, and its AI video and image generator, Adobe Firefly, in ChatGPT. It’s positioning the partnership as a way to “better understand how ads can provide helpful, relevant experiences” as it ramps up its own platform designed to help advertisers show up in AI search results. Williams-Sonoma You might see ads for Williams-Sonoma’s range of housewares, kitchenware, furniture, and other products, too. The company says it’s going to explore how ads in ChatGPT will help “surface relevant, high-quality products” at “decision-making moments.” Audible It looks like ChatGPT’s ads won’t be limited to tangible products, either, as the Amazon-owned Audible plans to work with OpenAI to “reach new audiobook listeners” through ChatGPT. It’s not clear whether Audible will only show ads for its subscription or if it will showcase specific audiobooks when someone asks ChatGPT for recommendations. HelloFresh The meal kit company HelloFresh is also bringing ads to ChatGPT. Patrick Stal, the company’s senior vice president of global marketing, says on LinkedIn that the partnership will allow the brand to offer a “solution” to customers using ChatGPT for things like meal planning. Ford, Mazda, Mrs. Myers, and more The advertising agency WPP Media is working with Ford, Mazda, the cleaning company Mrs. Myers, and the luxury Swiss watch company Audemars Piguet to launch ads in ChatGPT as well. (Its other clients include Audible and Adobe, too). Meanwhile, other agencies, including Dentsu and Omnicom, have announced that they’re going to bring their clients’ ads to ChatGPT as well, though they don’t specify which brands are involved. Instead, Dentsu notes that it has “several clients” participating in OpenAI’s test across grocery, hospitality, retail, software, travel, and the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industries, which could include items like food and beverages, cosmetics, or cleaning products. Omnicom lists companies specializing in apparel, automotive, beauty, CPG, technology, telecommunications, hospitality, retail, and fast-food as participants in OpenAI’s test. Update, February 11th: Added HelloFresh.

articles.title: IAs da OpenAI enfraquecem sistema criado para monitorá-las | G1
articles.standfirst: Em um dos casos, modelo retirou um mecanismo de segurança e depois afirmou incorretamente que não havia feito isso.
articles.summary: Em um dos casos, modelo retirou um mecanismo de segurança e depois afirmou incorretamente que não havia feito isso.
articles.body:
As preocupações que levaram a OpenAI, do ChatGPT, a abandonar lançamento de novo sistema de IA — Foto: Andrej Ivanov/AFP via Getty Images

A OpenAI informou que dois de seus agentes de inteligência artificial (IA) enfraqueceram sistemas de segurança usados pela empresa para monitorar as ações dos próprios modelos. Os casos ocorreram durante tarefas internas de programação.

Esse é o caso mais recente de agentes de IA que agiram de maneiras não previstas por seus desenvolvedores.

Embora a empresa responsável pelo ChatGPT tenha afirmado que os incidentes ocorreram durante tarefas internas de programação e não foram classificados entre os casos mais graves, os episódios mostram que até os sistemas criados para detectar comportamentos inadequados da IA podem sofrer interferência dos próprios agentes que monitoram.

A revelação ocorre em meio a preocupações crescentes de que os avanços na segurança da IA não acompanhem o ritmo de desenvolvimento de sistemas cada vez mais poderosos. Pesquisadores têm alertado que agentes avançados podem se tornar mais difíceis de monitorar e controlar à medida que ganham autonomia.

Empresas como OpenAI e Anthropic, rivais que se preparam para abrir o capital, revelaram nos últimos meses casos em que agentes de IA acessaram sistemas externos sem autorização.

Em 3 de outubro, um agente GPT-6.1 Sol que realizava um teste interno desativou alertas automáticos de segurança após interpretar que uma instrução anterior para não enviar mensagens pelo Slack também se aplicava às notificações de segurança, segundo a OpenAI.

Em outro episódio, em 6 de outubro, um agente GPT-6 Astra removeu um mecanismo de monitoramento de segurança enquanto copiava um código existente e depois afirmou, incorretamente, que não havia feito isso, segundo a OpenAI.

“Em ambos os casos, os agentes avaliaram se os mecanismos de monitoramento deveriam ser mantidos, mas interpretaram instruções rotineiras de programação como permissão para enfraquecê-los”, afirmou a empresa.

A OpenAI afirmou que está adotando medidas para dificultar que os modelos desativem os mecanismos de monitoramento, mas admitiu que “ainda não tem uma explicação satisfatória para esse comportamento”.

A empresa também está investigando se seus modelos podem ter uma tendência a evitar o monitoramento e buscar justificativas para fazer isso.

articles.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
articles.summary: After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users.
articles.body: After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users. The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with “rollout happening globally too,” according to Google (we’ve asked for specific regional availability details). It’s taken almost 12 months for Google to bring this to CarPlay users, but now they can talk to the voice assistant in Google Maps to get some hands-free help while driving. That includes asking it multi-step questions, such as recommendations on places to visit and then prompting it to direct you there while avoiding toll roads. Users can activate the feature by tapping the Gemini icon in Google Maps on their Car’s infotainment display. Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go. There’s no mention of any of the Personal Intelligence features that were announced yesterday for Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, however, which enable the voice assistant to access user information from Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. We’ve asked Google if CarPlay users will also receive the personalization update and will update if we hear back.

articles.title: Who's paying for the AI build-out? Probably you
articles.summary: What was the cost of the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a percentage of the Fourth Dynasty's GDP? It is unlikely that Pharaoh Khufu thought in those...
articles.body:
What was the cost of the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a percentage of the Fourth Dynasty's GDP? It is unlikely that Pharaoh Khufu thought in those terms, and the accounts have been lost over the intervening 4,600 years. The question is topical nonetheless, as America is building a 21st-century equivalent: an AI data centre network that dwarfs all of its previous infrastructure efforts.

Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh of Brookings estimates the AI infrastructure boom will cost the equivalent of 3.6 per cent of US GDP a year over the eight-year period ending in 2032 — equalling the annual spending on the railroad boom of the late 19th century, plus the interstate highway projects of the mid-20th century, plus about two-thirds of the electrification spending of the early 20th century. Total bill: $10.3tn, an estimate including only tangible expenditures, not intangibles such as software.

Who pays? Substantially all of the profits of some of the world's most profitable companies — the so-called hyperscalers — have been staked. Add to this the new debt these mega-companies are taking on directly or guaranteeing, supplemented by more speculative debt and equity financing for smaller companies. Almost every big pool of capital, from every corner of the developed world, has been tapped. In short, if you have invested savings, you are financing the AI build-out.

The details are not easy to nail down, but hyperscalers' direct investments are the most transparent. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX are expected to generate $760bn in cash flow this year. All of this and more will be invested, meaning "free cash flow" will be negative, a situation Wall Street expects to persist for several years, even as profits at the companies are projected to grow at a breakneck 30 per cent a year.

Equity investors can console themselves with the idea that a big chunk of the hyperscalers' investment converts into profits at semiconductor companies. But remember that these companies are investing heavily, too: capital expenditures at the 30 largest are set to pass $200bn this year, double the level of three years ago, and to grow from there.

There is another layer of financing flowing from the hyperscalers and chipmakers: equity investments in AI labs and other AI start-ups. Nvidia, for example, carries $94bn in private and public equity investments on its balance sheet, including stakes in OpenAI, Anthropic and CoreWeave. In a gold rush, it is often said, the real profits are made selling picks and shovels. In the AI gold rush, the shovel companies are investing part of their profits to buy mines.

articles.title: GPT‑5.6 Sol was used to identify critical PHP flaw.
articles.summary:
OpenAI says a security researcher at Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol to identify PHP exploits before attackers did, and has shared a tool that lets developers check if they’re using a potentially vulnerable version of PHP that needs patching. Ami Luttwak, co-founder of Google’s Wiz security team that also helped to identidy the PHP2Shell exploit, told the Wall Street Journal that its “the most severe AI vulnerability that was ever found.”

articles.title: PHP armageddon: OpenAI, Google's Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: This is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented by AI, but is also a high risk because of AI.
articles.body:
The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation .

PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites . It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress.

The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app.

Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.

So how did two such ubiquitous, decades-old flaws that affect nearly every website on the internet suddenly come to light? AI, naturally, particularly via OpenAI and Google’s Wiz.

Security testing company Calif was engaged in OpenAI’s “Patch the Planet” initiative to find flaws in open-source source software. Using GPT‑5.6 Sol, it found one of the flaws, OpenAI disclosed in a blog post . Separately, the Wiz team also used AI, namely its Wiz Atlas security AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities in PHP.

Both OpenAI and Wiz followed responsible security research practices and worked with PHP on patches before publicly disclosing the flaws. Then they all worked together to flesh out what they found, and test the patches, drawing in a host of others to help.

Wiz thanked Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare, Fastly, Imperva, Microsoft, and Vercel. (While WordPress sites use PHP, WordPress has issued a statement saying that the flaw isn’t WordPress specific, and sites running its CMS must patch their servers and work with their web-hosting companies to ensure their sites are protected.)

OpenAI says that these flaws were found by researchers before hackers discovered them. So there were no reports of exploits in the wild. This is also in part because, before AI, these flaws were too hard for hackers to exploit. “With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts,” Wiz warned in its blog about the flaws.

In other words, this is the kind of security issue that was found and prevented because of AI, but is also a high risk only because of AI.

Now that the issue has been disclosed, hackers are fully in the know. The race is on for the internet to patch tens millions of websites before hackers can attack the unpatched ones. Hence the NSA’s guidance that if you can’t patch your PHP website right away, you’re better off pulling it offline until you can.

articles.title: GM is giving OnStar an AI makeover
articles.summary: It's one of the biggest overhauls ever to the 30-year-old connected car product.
articles.body:
General Motors is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar as part of a broader makeover of the subscription-based connected car service that the U.S. automaker launched 30 years ago.

The OnStar AI Assistant will debut in the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV in the coming months, with more GM vehicles to follow, the company said Wednesday at its GM Forward event in New York, where it made a series of other technology announcements covering software, automated driving, EVs, and its electrical architecture. The company said it will launch a new OnStar mobile app in 2027 that will complement and sync up with its in-car software.

The new OnStar mobile app will replace the current OnStar Guardian app that launched in 2020 as well as vehicle brand apps for Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC.

This tech-centric reboot is unlike other attempts to modernize OnStar and it notably puts agentic AI at the center. The company has updated the safety and roadside assistance service numerous times in its history, especially in the past five years as it tried to stay apace of emerging and tech-forward competitors like Tesla.

In 2021, the company expanded its OnStar Guardian app, which offered crash detection, emergency assistance and location sharing, to anyone with a compatible phone, even if they didn’t own a GM vehicle. A year later, GM started using Google Cloud’s conversational AI Dialogflow to recognize specific spoken requests and expanded in 2023 to give drivers responses to common queries like routing and navigation assistance — all part of GM’s plan to build a $25 billion subscription business by 2030 .

GM continued to focus on generative AI, but relied on Google to provide the experience. The company said last year that Google Gemini would roll out in vehicles in 2026.

The OnStar AI Assistant is an in-house effort and one aimed at giving the driver and passengers an interactive and custom experience — and become even more embedded in their daily lives.

“OnStar is now transitioning to be a connected intelligence platform, not just the call center that it’s historically been known as, but a mechanism for interpreting, understanding, and providing predictive, proactive support to its owners,” GM’s VP of global product and chief product officer Sterling Anderson told TechCrunch in an interview ahead of the GM Forward event.

For instance, cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users can set up the connected cameras to turn on automatically if the vehicle senses an impending event — for instance an aggressive horn honk — then capture the event and upload it to the OnStar app. Users will be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.

The launch coincides with efforts throughout the auto industry to stay apace of Chinese automakers with technology that is central to the vehicle — and no longer a slapped on gimmick or feature. But that has required GM to change its approach to software development, adopt AI tools, and even design a new electrical and centralized compute vehicle architecture.

The announcement also comes after GM has been criticized and even fined for sharing data with third parties. Earlier this year, the Federal Trade Commission finalized an order that bans General Motors and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data with consumer reporting agencies. The finalized order also requires the automaker to be more transparent with its consumers and obtain their explicit consent on certain data collection.

GM said Wednesday that customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared, and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings.

A GM spokesperson later shared that third-party sharing a “feature-specific and consent-based, with information shared only as needed to provide requested functionality.” Customers can manage permissions and withdraw consent, however those who choose not to share certain data may have limited access to related features, while other OnStar services would continue, according to GM.
